host.list.title: Hosts
host.col.name: Name
host.form.name: Host name
host.form.nameHint: The name is the external identifier (the hostId in URLs) and cannot be changed later.
host.form.nameImmutable: The host name cannot be changed: it is the external identifier, and renaming breaks shared links.
host.form.endpointSocketHint: A local socket endpoint starts with /, e.g. /var/run/docker.sock
host.form.endpointTcpHint: A remote endpoint starts with tcp:// or https:// and includes a port
host.form.authHint: TLS and Basic are mutually exclusive; selecting neither means no auth.
host.form.authEditHint: When editing, leaving these empty keeps the stored credentials; switching to \"no auth\" clears them.
host.form.tlsNote: These are **file paths visible inside the container**, not certificate contents; all three are required (a missing CA means accepting any server certificate).
host.form.testOk: Connected: this configuration reaches the daemon.
host.form.testFailed: Cannot connect: check the endpoint, the credentials and whether the target host is reachable.
host.disable.title: Disable host
host.disable.impact: Once disabled, every resource request targeting this host is rejected (1302) and its container / image pages become unavailable.
host.empty: No hosts registered yet — add the first one.
host.confirm.delete.title: Delete host
host.confirm.delete.soft: Deletion is soft: the name is released and can be registered again.
host.group.listHint: Groups only affect how the overview page is laid out — they grant nothing.
host.group.name: Group name
host.group.nameHint: The three built-in groups use English identifiers (production / staging / local) and are shown translated; custom groups appear exactly as you type them.
host.group.descriptionPlaceholder: Optional one-liner about what these machines are for
host.group.descriptionHint: Leave empty to clear the description.
host.group.confirm.delete.title: Delete group
host.group.confirm.delete.keepHosts: Hosts in this group are not deleted — they simply return to \"ungrouped\".

page.users.subtitle: Create accounts, assign roles, or reset someone else's password. Resource-level authorization lands in 0.3.0.
page.users.title: User and role management
user.empty: No other users yet — create the first one.
user.footnote: Deletion is soft: the username is released and can be reused. Both deletion and password reset revoke every session of that user.
user.create.title: New user
user.form.usernameInvalid: Username must be 3–32 chars using letters, digits and _ . - only
user.form.passwordPlaceholder: At least 10 chars with letters and digits or symbols
user.form.passwordHint: At least 10 characters, including letters plus digits or symbols.
user.form.passwordWeak: Password needs at least 10 characters with letters plus digits or symbols
user.form.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match
user.form.passwordSame: The new password equals the old one — that changes nothing
user.form.roleNamePlaceholder: A role that already exists on the server
user.form.roleNameHint: The name must match an existing role; an unknown name returns "role not found".
user.reset.title: Reset password
user.reset.for: Set a new password for "{name}" (no current password needed).
user.reset.warning: All sessions of this user are revoked; they must sign in again with the new password.
user.reset.done: Password for "{name}" reset; all their sessions were revoked
user.change.title: Change password
user.change.warning: You will need to sign in again (all sessions are revoked).
user.change.done: Password changed — please sign in with the new one
user.delete.selfHint: You cannot delete the account you are signed in with
user.confirm.delete.title: Delete user
user.confirm.delete.sessions: All sessions of this user are revoked; they must sign in again.
user.confirm.delete.soft: Deletion is soft: the username is released and can be reused.
page.users.note: Admin only; depends on the user management API (0.0.8). Resource-level authorization follows in 0.3.0.

page.events.note: Requires an audit table first; docs/features.md schedules it after 1.0.0. Note this is platform operation auditing, not the Docker Events stream.
